sources: recreation.gov campsite catalog for 232073 (search/campsites API, read 2026-10-28)

values.note: $30 per site; $33 at sites 4-10, 12 and 13 (same in recreation.gov's 2026-2028 tables). Two vehicles or one RV included; $11 a night for a third vehicle (boat/ATV trailers count as one).

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/molly-brown-campground ('$30 fee per site for overnight camping. $33 fee for overnight camping at sites 4-10, 12 and 13. Two vehicles or one recreational vehicle are included in the camping fee. $11 fee for a third vehicle') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232073/rates (2026, 2027, 2028 Peak Season: STANDARD NONELECTRIC 30, premium STANDARD NONELECTRIC 33), read 2026-10-28

hookups.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232073 (notice 'No hookups available') + catalog 232073 (all sites NONELECTRIC), read 2026-10-28

values.note: 43 back-in RV/tent sites catalogued at 20-40 ft (eight at 20 ft, the rest 25-40) plus 2 tent-only sites, on two loops. Every vehicle must fit on the spur, no parking on the grass. One RV and two tents, or three tents, per site; 8 people max.

sites.source: recreation.gov catalog 232073 (43 STANDARD NONELECTRIC, Max Vehicle Length 20 x8, 25 x7, 30 x9, 35 x11, 40 x8, all Back-In; 2 TENT ONLY) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232073 ('The two-loop campground offers single family sites'; 'all vehicles must fit in the parking spur. Please no parking on the grass'; '3 tent maximum per site, or 1 RV and 2 tents'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: No water in 2026 - bring your own, including enough to put out a campfire; the campground normally has potable water. The White Star and Printer Boy RV dump stations are closed for 2026. Trash collection; firewood $10 a bundle at the host site.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/molly-brown-campground ('Vault toilets are located throughout the campground'; 'Potable water is not available at this site. Water will not be available in this campground in 2026') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232073 (notices 'Water will NOT be available in this campground in 2026 ... the RV Dump Stations at both Printer Boy & White Star Campgrounds will remain closed this season', 'Firewood is available for sale at host site for $10.00/bundle'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: May to September; opening and closing dates are weather dependent, and water, trash or a host may be missing early and late in the season.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/molly-brown-campground ('Seasons of Use: May to September. Opening and closing dates are weather dependent. Services such as water, trash or a host may not be available during early and late season.'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: All sites are reservable on recreation.gov or 877-444-6777 at least four days ahead; walk-ups take what is left (the FS page says walk-ups are exempt from the weekend minimum, and a first-come site must be occupied the first night). Reservation season 2026 May 22 - Sept 19; recreation.gov's 2027 table runs May 21 - Sept 5.

note: USFS (Pike-San Isabel NF, Leadville Ranger District), concessionaire-run, on the east shore of Turquoise Lake at 9,900 ft in shaded lodgepole pine, about 5 mi west of Leadville via County Road 4 and County Road 9C. The Turquoise Lake Nature Trail crosses to Silver Dollar Campground and loops along the shore. --Claude
summary: FS + rec.gov + catalog: confirmed 45 sites, max 40 ft (catalog), no hookups, reservable on recreation.gov, $30 base. Added $33 high (sites 4-10, 12, 13), all back-in, vault toilets, no water in 2026, season May-Sept (note), fcfs after_cutoff with 4-day cutoff, 14-night limit, booking.season 05-22..09-19, senior/access 50%. Note rewritten (it said 'Turquoise/Twin Lakes' and repeated fields). Min-stay not recorded (FS states it, rec.gov rules do not).
flags: Missing phone: Leadville Ranger District 719-486-0749 (FS page office contact; recreation.gov lists the same number 'FOR INFORMATION ONLY, NO RESERVATIONS'). recreation.gov's facility-specific line is (661) 702-1420 (concessionaire, goexplorus.com).
Website: recreation.gov only; add the FS page https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/molly-brown-campground.

Access: PSICC alert 'Turquoise Lake Road (County Road 4) Closure' (since April 7, 2026): CR 4 'is barricaded from the Abe Lee parking turnoff to Hagerman Pass. Access to Turquoise Lake is still available via County Road 9C and County Road 9'. Molly Brown is reached from Leadville west on CR 4 then right on CR 9C (recreation.gov directions), the east end of the lake, short of the barricade - so it stays reachable by CR 4 (east of Abe Lee) and CR 9C.

Closure order: Willow Fire Area Closure 02-12-01-26-39 (Oct 1 - Dec 31, 2026) closes NFS lands 'South of Turquoise Lake ... to the South of Lake County Road 4 and NFSR 105 (Hagerman Pass Road)' and on to Halfmoon Creek. Molly Brown is on the east shore north of CR 4, up CR 9C, so it is outside the described area as worded. The campground's season is over anyway; not a status.

Waterfront (stored not waterfront) - contrary claim, re-audit lead (not changed): recreation.gov says 'Campsites are perched along the scenic waters of the lake' and 'on the eastern shore of Turquoise Lake'. On Esri imagery with the catalog points, the nearest sites (the west row, roughly 011-019) sit ~60-90 m inside continuous lodgepole forest from the forest edge at the top of the beach (full-pool line; the photo shows a wide drawn-down sand band below it); the rest are 150-300 m back. No open apron to the water. At most a view through trees from the west row.

Minimum stay conflict: the FS page says a Friday+Saturday stay is required on weekends and three nights on holiday weekends (walk-ups exempt), but recreation.gov's facility rules for 232073 carry no minimum (only maxConsecutiveStay 14 and the 4-day cutoff). Not recorded, as at Father Dyer (2412).
Length: neither the FS page nor recreation.gov's description states a maximum; catalog per-site 20-40 ft, with 35 of 43 RV sites at 25 ft or more. Kept 40 (real per-site values, not a placeholder).

Pin 39.26639,-106.34972 (recreation.gov facility point) is ~433 m NE of the 45 site points' centroid (39.26383,-106.35351), in the open meadow east of the loops. Under 500 m, but the FS page's coordinate 39.26436,-106.35238 sits within ~110 m of the centroid - suggest re-pinning there.
Fee: FS and recreation.gov agree ($30 / $33). rating.price_tier 1 (RV Life 2026-06) is RV Life's and was not changed.
